My goal is to maximize my outcome in the deferred acceptance algorithm. My values are z > x > w > y, and my priorities are w:1, x:2, y:1, z:2.

Since I have top priority at w and y, I am very likely to get into either of those if I rank them highly. I have lower priority at x and z, so I am less likely to get into those if I rank them highly, especially if others are ranking y > x > w > z.

I want to avoid dominated strategies. I should always rank my favorite school first, which is z. If I don't get z, my next best options are x, w, and y. I have high priority at w and y, so I should rank them higher than x to ensure I have a good chance of getting into those. Since w is more valuable than y, I should rank w before y.

Therefore, my ranking should be z > w > y > x.

- If I rank x first, I might get x. But if I rank z first, I might get z, which is better.
- If I rank y first, I might get y. But if I rank z first, I might get z, which is better.

Therefore, ranking z first is undominated.

Given that most applicants favor y > x > w > z, this reinforces my strategy to rank z and x high, since they are likely to be less competitive.
